question: Did something change with elections recently? My snap election fired at a different time than I expected.
answer:
Yes — a fix shipped yesterday (27 August) that changed *when* snap elections fire. The game had been scheduling an election whenever a country's system converted (a Stage 4 regime collapse or a voluntary constitutional convention) but never actually running it. Two fixes went live yesterday: the promised post-conversion election now actually fires (e6538a64b), and the step that fires it runs every turn (b678cd3ab). So if your country went through a conversion, a snap now fires on the first post-conversion turn where it previously never would have fired at all — that is the most likely cause of the timing you didn't expect.

Two related snap changes shipped the same day:

| Change | Effect on timing |
|---|---|
| Regime changes can now dissolve any legislature (ef3529cd9) | A snap can fire in countries that don't normally allow them |
| Imposed snaps keep the LARP calendar canonical (1bbda4601) | An imposed snap doesn't push the next regular election later, while a PM-called snap does |

If you called the snap yourself, nothing about its timing changed: it starts immediately with a 48-hour window (24h primary + 24h general). The timing shift comes from the post-conversion path, not the PM button. Check your country's event feed — a headline reading "Dissolved Under a Peace Settlement" means an imposed snap fired; "…Dissolves …" means it was the executive's own call.

question: Why did my stocks fall this week? Was it a code change?
correctionsInjected: Show how my own savings and wealth changed over recent turns. Visualize the largest change.
answer:
## Likely cause: market movement, not a patch

Nothing shipped to the live game in the last 45 days touches personal stock holdings or your portfolio's stock-value calculation. The four commits in your recent-change list that mention "stock" all do something else:

- [PR #1039](https://github.com/Egg3901/AHDGame/commit/7ff9fc20db4e6f23e1123f88775492bea9d68a18) caps an index-fund capital-book anchor and adds an insolvency materiality floor.
- [PR #1035](https://github.com/Egg3901/AHDGame/commit/5745adba7598930bb519e9e018a220f58b3c938e) changes how NPPs expand owned plants.
- [PR #1062](https://github.com/Egg3901/AHDGame/commit/fff8e309e2c11c54292a1366e0eb8da7d248c593) de-duplicates Discord news webhooks.
- [PR #1059](https://github.com/Egg3901/AHDGame/commit/3e4956a941a2619aff14640942d82667504148a7) adds a Senate confirmation vote UI for the FOMC committee.

None of those edit the stock-price engine, the personal-portfolio calculator in `src/app/portfolio/PortfolioClient.tsx`, or the breakdown chart in `src/components/charts/PortfolioBreakdownChart.tsx`. So a code change is not the explanation.

## What actually moves your stock line

Your portfolio's stocks series (`stockValue` in the history points) tracks the mark-to-market value of the equities you hold, so the line moves for ordinary market reasons:

- The listed share price of Tinky Winky Corporation or any other stock you own drifted this turn.
- Other players or NPPs bought or sold, moving the order book.
- An underlying corporation's fundamentals (sector NPVs, debt, earnings forecast) shifted, which feeds the blended fair-value model that sets the quote.

> A falling "Stocks" line on your breakdown chart is the same number the public exchange shows for those tickers, recomputed at turn close — it is not a personal-account glitch.

## How to see exactly what changed

Open the **Stocks** tab on your portfolio page; it shows the current position count and mark-to-market for each holding. The exchange page for each ticker (linked from there) shows the live quote and recent price history, so you can see whether the move was in the price or in the quantity (a sale, a transfer, or a corporate action).

question: Why did my approval suddenly drop after I passed a popular bill?
answer:
Approvals move from several systems at once, so a drop right after a bill passes is almost never the bill itself — it's something the bill's passage triggered. The most common culprits, in order of likelihood:

## The bill's side effect, not the bill

- **Budget-pass path.** If the bill is the annual Budget, the UK confidence gauge (PR #901, live 2026-08-25) treats passing it as a **+10** confidence event but does **not** stop the per-turn confidence drift from the government's standing approval. If your national approval is below the 50 pivot at the moment of passage, the gauge still erodes and can drag the visible standing-approval metrics down with it.
- **Nationalization / privatization consequences.** A bill that takes a private firm, or sells one, runs through the political-cost math in `src/lib/nationalization/consequences/compute.ts`. A "popular" framing still applies a public-trust nudge scaled by **ideology multiplier** and **concentration multiplier** — past the danger zone of state ownership, that boost **flips negative** (the public sours on a state that owns too much). So a well-liked seizing bill on top of an already-large state sector can read as a loss.
- **Crisis-aid pledge.** A head-of-state aid commitment creates a `CrisisAidCommitment` (`src/lib/db/types/crisisAid.ts`). When the legislature votes it, the *sender's* approval takes the diplomatic effects, and a **failed** vote writes an `approvalPenaltyExpiresTurn` on the sender. If the bill is the aid package and a coalition partner defected, that's where the drop comes from.
- **Westminster rework (PR #901, 2026-08-25).** The UK now has an explicit confidence gauge that bottoms out at 0 to trigger dissolution, and a **broken-promise bleed** that continuously drains the gauge when manifesto delivery slips. Passing a bill that *contradicts* a manifesto commitment feeds the meter and bleeds confidence every turn.

## Quick diagnostic

| Signal in the newswire | Likely source |
|---|---|
| Drop on same turn as a Budget pass | Confidence gauge drift below 50 pivot |
| Drop after a nationalization/privatization | `compute.ts` approval nudge × ideology/concentration |
| Drop after an aid-package vote | `CrisisAidCommitment.senderEffects` on a failed vote |
| Slow bleed over the next turns after passing | Broken-promise bleed from manifesto delivery |

> The bill's title doesn't tell you its effect class. Open the bill card and check whether it's tagged as a Budget, an economic-action (nationalize/privatize), or a crisis-aid pledge — that tag picks which consequence module ran.
